strata-caverns.look: The void view is unlike anything on the existing sheet: stacked horizontal galleries with dead-flat floors and domed, lobed ceilings, separated by rock and linked by short vertical shafts; the cut faces show it as rows of lens voids like limestone bedding planes. Cave view: level galleries carved into the cube with flat floors you could walk on, shaft holes in the roof. 2D sheet: rows of flat-bottomed lenses with vertical pits between rows. Coverage controls the look from isolated pockets (cov -0.2) to continuous halls with pillars (cov 0.4); cov -0.1 gives room-and-pillar. Connectivity (6^3 box): defaults 14 components, largest 76.7%; with S=1.5, ps=0.9, cov=0.25, height=0.6 it is 98.6% one component (7 components, no sealed pockets); pillar setting 52.8% (layers are only joined where a shaft happens to land in open plan on both sides). In-plane warp 0.4 barely changes the look because floors stay flat by design. y is privileged, that is the point.
strata-caverns.dims: 2D (XY section with a 1D plan) and 3D measured; 4D would feed w to the plan source only, not attempted
strata-caverns.range: [-1, 1], flat at +1 in rock beyond dmax = min(base-0.04, 1-base-height)*H (0.16 with the chosen params), no NaN, far coords fine. Max slope 24 per unit at the shaft/dome junctions (smin), continuous.
strata-caverns.artifacts: sqrt dome regularised with e=0.02 so walls are steep but finite. Shafts are cylinders with hard ends. Without smask most shafts land in rock; with it shafts become rare where coverage is low, hence the poorly connected pillar setting. The XZ sheet slice usually lands in rock between galleries so only shaft dots show.
strata-caverns.node_shape: StrataCaverns: Plan (GeneratorSource sampled at a slab-snapped y), Layer Height, Floor, Height, Coverage (hybrid), Gain, Shaft Spacing, Shaft Radius (hybrid), Shaft Chance, Shaft Mask (bool), Output Min/Max.
strata-caverns.port_notes: No window: one slab hash, two boundary hashes, one macro cell. Plan evaluated with the source at (x + ox_j, j*137, z + oz_j). Shaft mask costs 4 extra source evals, make it optional. Continuity needs base*H >= dmax and (1-base-height)*H >= dmax: clamp dmax from the params. Dip (tilt) hybrid from the idea is a one-line addition, not prototyped.

critic.notes: Best look in the family and the only one with walkable floors; it holds on seeds 99, 7, 2024 and at window 12. Recommended params: 100.0 and 97.4% in 6^3, 100.00% in the core of 12^3 on 3 seeds. The defaults are much weaker: 51.1% in 6^3 on seed 99 (reported 76.7%), pillar setting 35.3% (reported 52.8%). The 'nothing else produces it' claim fails: the graph recipe already on disk, which I re-ran and did not write, gives the same floors, domes, per layer plans and shafts on my seeds, and with y warp and dip the window 12 cave views are hard to tell apart. Graph costs: 32.06 ns AVX2 3D, 33.92 with y warp and dip (both measured), 40 nodes in tree form, fatter shafts with blunt blind ends in rock since it has no shaft mask, 92.9-96.0% in 6^3 with 1.2-1.45% of the cave sealed. A node would be about 15 ns with a 2D plan call, about 26 ns with a 3D plan call and the mask on (my estimates, not measured). So a node would be easier and somewhat faster, but for one y privileged look a preset is enough. Closest call in the family; layer height being spread over several constants is the real weakness of the preset. Scalar 18.92x perlin2 under the harness, higher than the reported 9.77x. c0ratio 6.72, max slope 20.6, shaft and dome junctions steep but no jump found.
critic.improved: The prototyper said no warp is needed since floors must stay flat. A warp that depends on y only (ya=1.6,yf=0.3) keeps floors dead flat and makes layer thickness vary, which removes the ruler; a low frequency y-only warp (dip=2.2,dipf=0.09) then tilts the beds. Cut faces now read as sedimentary bedding. Connectivity unchanged, 99.98-100.00% in the core of 12^3 on seeds 99 and 7. Both are real nodes upstream: DomainOffset Y fed by a Perlin with Scaling X = Z = 0, and DomainWarpGradient with Amplitude Scaling X = Z = 0. Added them to the existing graph recipe and rendered it.

master.one_liner: Karst-style cavern layers: per-slab 2D cave plans with flat floors and domed ceilings, separated by rock and linked by hashed vertical shafts.
master.look: Not prototyped. Vertical (XY) slice: stacked flat-bottomed lens voids in rows like limestone bedding planes. Horizontal (XZ) slice: island-and-pillar plans (room-and-pillar). 3D iso: horizontal galleries with level floors, walkable, joined by vertical pits. Different from all blob caves, which have no flat floors. For game levels, limestone, salt mines.
master.algorithm: Slab coordinate y' = y/H + Dip*Tilt(x,z) from an optional hybrid. j = floor(y'), t = y' - j. Slab hash gives lateral offset (ox,oz). Plan value n = Source(x+ox, j*137.0, z+oz) evaluated at a snapped y so it is constant through the slab. Openness a = sat(n*g + Coverage). Floor tf = Base + small hash shift. Ceiling tc = tf + Height * sqrt(a) (domed, vertical at walls). dv = max(tf - t, t - tc) * H (positive = rock, a = 0 gives tc=tf, so rock). Shafts: for boundary indices j and j+1, macro-cell (floor(x/S), floor(z/S)) hash gives centre, r, presence; ds = max(cylinder distance, span distance around boundary). d = smin(dv, ds). Output ScaleOutput(min(d, Dmax)). Continuity at slab boundaries needs Base*H >= Dmax and (1 - Base - Height)*H >= Dmax. Connectivity within a slab: in 2D a symmetric field's level set percolates exactly when coverage exceeds 50% (Zallen-Scher, proven for Gaussian fields), so Coverage just above 0 gives one giant horizontal cavern with pillars, by a known theorem, not by luck. Dense shafts link slabs.
master.why_new: Every noise cave is isotropic blobby and not walkable. Flat floors and horizontal layering need a floor(y) snapped source position, not available in a graph (no quantise-domain node). Terrace only remaps values. Controlled by designer-level parameters like layer height and coverage.
master.simd_plan: 1 source eval, 1 slab hash, 2 shaft hashes, then a few mins and one sqrt; no window. 3D: Source cost + 1.5 ns; 2D (x,y) uses 1D plan. 4D: extra axis to source (morphing plan over w). Slab offset is converted to int via bit field; Select-free except for presence mask. Far cheaper than a volumetric fractal.
master.continuity: C0, by the boundary rule above; rock is flat at Dmax beyond the band. Sqrt dome has infinite ceiling slope at a=0 which makes vertical walls; regularise by sqrt(a+e)-sqrt(e).
master.params: Source (plan), Layer Height H, Base, Height, Coverage (hybrid), Gain g, Shaft Spacing S, Shaft Radius (hybrid), Dip (hybrid optional), Dmax.
master.risks: Untested. y is privileged. Shaft may not land in a cavern; density must be high, or use shaft mask by plan value at centre (one extra source eval per shaft). 50% percolation holds for symmetric fields; Perlin is close but not exact and near threshold connections are thin. Walkable look depends on height vs feature scale.

bond-tunnels.look: Unwarped 3D pipes view: plumbing, straight axis-aligned tubes with elbows at the jittered ports and hubs, bulbs where chamber > 0, obviously a cubic lattice. Rotation alone removes the axis alignment but the regular knot spacing still reads as a grid. A fine warp (0.3 at freq 1.2) bends the tubes but keeps straight-ish runs; adding a coarse warp (1.2 at freq 0.2) turns it into a woven root or vessel mass with no visible straight lines, though a regular weave density remains. Cave view: oval tunnel cross sections on the cut faces, nothing else to see. 2D: a blocky maze of corridors with dead ends; warp 0.3 at freq 1.2 removes the right angles, 0.5 starts to pinch corridors. Connectivity in a 6^3 box: percolation p=0.6 99.1% of the cave in one component (23 components, mostly tiny orphan stubs), with chambers 99.3%, p=0.4 95.2%; the full warped 8^3 config 99.6% with one pinched voxel pocket. Tree mode is honest but disappointing in-view: 73 components, largest 11.9%, because the directed forest only coalesces far away. A vertical parent bias (tree, ybias=6) with warp gives hanging root strands, saved as a discovery.
bond-tunnels.dims: 2D and 3D measured (generic n-dim code); 4D is the same loop over 8 faces, not run
bond-tunnels.range: [-1, 1] over 8 seeds, rock flat at +1 beyond dmax = min(stub, 0.5 - max(jit,hub) - rmax) - smooth (0.17 with the chosen params), no NaN, far coords fine, 3D z-continuity max 0.006 per 1e-3
bond-tunnels.artifacts: none at the seam-rule bound; smooth-min near a face can leak up to smooth/4 across cells so dmax is reduced by smooth. The XZ slice is a lattice of dots unless warped. Tube radius capped near 0.2 cells by the bound, fat caves need Feature Scale.
bond-tunnels.node_shape: BondTunnels: Feature Scale, Link enum {Percolation, Tree, Both} (absorbs spanning-tunnels), Bond Chance (hybrid), Port Jitter, Hub Jitter, Stub, Radius Min/Max (hybrid), Chamber (hybrid), Smooth, Vertical Bias, Output Min/Max; clamped signed distance output (rock +). Graph: DomainRotate + DomainWarpFractalProgressive (2 octaves) upstream.
bond-tunnels.port_notes: One cell window: cell hash + 2n face hashes keyed on the +side cell and axis so both cells agree; face carries open flag, port, radius. Tree mode needs n extra neighbour hashes. All arms evaluated unconditionally and masked to +big when closed. Percolation p above the lattice threshold (3D 0.249, 2D 0.5) gives a giant cluster; orphan pieces are rare. Connectivity tool: NETCONN env var.

critic.notes: Ship as the structured network node, not as the default cave. What it alone gives: the unwarped corridor maze in 2D and rectilinear plumbing or mine workings in 3D, chambers and dead ends, and connection at very low void: 100.00% in the core at 2.4-2.5% void, 99.27% at 1.4%, where the real noodle graph has fallen apart (0.13-6.43% at 2.5%) and F3-F1 too (0.00%). What it does not give: a better natural cave. Warped at 11% void it reads as a tangle with flakes, and the real graph Add(a^2, b^2) of two Perlin looks more organic with no lattice and no warp, 99.99-100.00% in the core at 9.29 ns measured, against 9.31 + 3.61 = 12.92 ns for bond plus warp, and F3-F1 is 99.99% at 11% void at 12.2-12.7 ns, faceted. So the 'only member both connected and cheap' claim fails against existing nodes above about 8% void. Connectivity: the reported 99.1-99.6% in a box is the wrong measure, box cuts count against it. Seeds 99 and 2024: 98.5 and 97.7% in 6^3, but 100.00% in the core of 11^3. p=.5 100.00 and 97.00, p=.45 97.5 and 97.9, p=.4 95.3 with 13 sealed pockets. It is statistical, not by construction, and the usable floor is p about 0.5. Warp costs some: amp 1 cell 98.16-99.93% in the core, 1.25 cells 96.21-99.87%, and thin tubes with warp 86.65% (they shear into ribbons near the voxel size, 16 voxels per cell). Do not make Bond Chance a HybridSource as proposed: sampled at the point it gives c0ratio 1.03, max slope 1851; at the face centre it is continuous but costs 2n source evals. Radius can be hybrid. 4D is not 'the same loop': through the 4D torus GenTileable2D uses it is isolated dots, and a flat 3D slice of the 4D net is fragments, so this node has no tiling and no w animation. Implement 2D and 3D and let 4D drop w. Radius capped near 0.2 cells by the bound, confirmed. Scalar 7.13x perlin2 under the harness with recommended params, the 2.52x headline was the tree default; AVX2 9.31 ns is 4.2x measured Perlin 3D.
critic.improved: Three things. (1) Measured the kernel: t_bond_avx2 is a direct AVX2 port, 9.31 ns/sample 3D with chamber and smooth min, 7.29 hard min, 7.25 without chamber, c0ratio 8.00 through the harness, so the 8-10 ns estimate holds. Port trap found on the way: a 1e6 sentinel for closed arms inside the smooth min loses float precision and gave c0ratio 1.00, max slope 368; a sentinel of 4 fixes it. (2) Restated the warp in real node terms with a scalar replica of DomainWarpGradient (rw=1), since the real node is hermite value noise with RMS 0.39 x amplitude vs 0.22 x for the prototype Perlin. (3) Two mutations. Mode 3 spine (macro lattice backbone plus parent paths, connected by construction) failed: same look as tree under warp, 97.9-99.4% in the core at M=4 and 78.5% at M=6, worse than p=0.6, code left in the proto. Two scale graph Min(coarse net, Max(fine net, low frequency mask)) works: it breaks the uniform density, 99.45-99.71% in the core, though coarse tubes turn slab-like under the same warp (estimate about 24 ns from measured parts).

master.one_liner: A cave network with a one-cell window: bond percolation on lattice faces, with hub and stub arms inside each cell, giving tubes that are connected by construction.
master.look: Prototyped in 2D and 3D. 3D isosurface: dense uniform pipe network with junctions. 2D: blocky maze with branching corridors and dead ends. 3D slice: clean round dots plus occasional stub traces. Needs DomainRotate and warp to look like caves rather than plumbing; with FlowWarp the topology stays guaranteed. Also pipes, roots, circuit, mycelium, mine levels.
master.algorithm: c=floor(p), f=p-c. Each cell face has a hash keyed by its lower cell and axis, so the two cells sharing it agree: open = rnd01(h) < BondP; port = face centre + J*rnd11 on the tangent axes. Cell hash gives hub = 0.5 + Jh*rnd11. For each of the 2*dim faces, if open: segments port -> inner (port moved Stub along the inward normal) and inner -> hub, distance d_arm = min of two segment distances; closed face: Select to Dmax. d = polynomial smin across arms. Output ScaleOutput(min(d, Dmax), 0, Dmax), and isosurface at Radius. Seamless because at a face only the shared perpendicular stub lies within Dmax of it, so Dmax <= Stub and J + Radius < 0.5. Percolation: cubic-lattice bond threshold is 0.2488, so BondP 0.5 to 0.6 gives a giant connected component with almost no orphans. Strict mode: each cell picks one parent among its 3 negative faces; low face open if the cell picked it, high face open if the neighbour across picked it (4 hashes). In 3D transverse walks are 2D and recurrent, so all paths coalesce into one tree, like the Scheidegger drainage model, with a provable connected network and no flood fill. Hybrid BondP: arm radius scales by sat((BondP(x)-rnd)/width), so bonds shrink instead of popping.
master.why_new: Connectivity guarantee is impossible with thresholded noise, and usually takes a flood fill. The trick of putting all information on faces reduces a segment network from 27 lattice cells and two hashes each to 1 cell and 7 hashes, so it is cheaper than a window search, with exact control of tube radius.
master.simd_plan: Fixed loop over 2*dim faces, Select by open mask, no window. Compare squared distances, take sqrt once if no smin. 3D: 7 hashes and 12 point-segment distances, estimate 7 to 10 ns, about 4x Perlin and well below CellularDistance. 2D about 2 ns; scalar prototype 1.66x perlin2. 4D: 9 hashes, 16 segments, about 15 ns versus 41 for CellularDistance, and a true 4D field for tiling; 4D tree mode gives a forest, not a tree, since transverse walks are transient there.
master.continuity: C0 everywhere (c0ratio 8.0, max slope 10 in the 2D sheet); C1 inside tubes when smin is used. Flat at Dmax in rock. Only near-surface values are distance-like, which is what caves use.
master.params: BondP (hybrid), Radius applied downstream or built in (hybrid), PortJitter, HubJitter, Stub, Dmax, Smooth, Mode enum: Percolation or Tree.
master.risks: Lattice signature is strong: axis-aligned stubs and grid dots in the FFT, axis ratio 64. It needs warp or rotation to look organic, and that is the main look risk. Tree mode has a global diagonal bias towards the negative corner. Very faint traces appear in slices when Dmax equals Stub, so use Dmax slightly below Stub.
master.cost_note: 3D: 7 hashes and 12 point-segment distances, estimate 7 to 10 ns, about 4x Perlin and well below CellularDistance.

queue.name: BondTunnels
queue.reason: Caves connected by construction from face-hash bond percolation in a 1-cell window, 4-8 ns in 3D (J4 top pick). Find how much warp hides the lattice signature.

truchet-noise.look: 2D: classic Smith-arc Truchet, smooth winding tubes that never end; warp 0.35 hides the square grid, 0.8 over-stretches it. The line-profile output (out=1) is a clean pipe/road pattern, and straight=0.2 adds crossings that make it a connected net. 3D vol: the cave view shows tube cross sections on the cut faces and a dense tangle of curved worm holes; axis aligned without rot/warp, organic with rot=1 plus warp 0.3. The pipes view (inv=1) is a dense mass of disjoint curved strands. The voxel flood fill at 6^3 cells found 55 separate components with the largest holding 3.5% of the cave (49 with fat tubes, 53 with straight pairings), so the 3D form is NOT a connected cave network: Truchet tubes never branch or meet, each strand is a closed loop or a wandering thread.
truchet-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 4D would drop w (generic n-dim code; an 8-face pairing table is possible but untested)
truchet-noise.range: [-0.78, 1.0] over 8 seeds, far coords fine, no NaN; flat at +1 in rock beyond dmax = 0.5 - rmax
truchet-noise.artifacts: initial signed-distance output had seams (c0ratio 1.1): the nearest tube at a face can be a non-exiting tube with a different radius; fixed by clamping at dmax = 0.5 - rmax (c0ratio 7.3 after). Straight axis-aligned runs show the lattice without a warp (axis ratio 143 unwarped, 91 at warp 0.35).
truchet-noise.node_shape: TruchetNoise: Feature Scale, Radius Min/Max (hybrid), Straight (0-1), Output enum {Signed, Lines, Stripes}, Line Width, Output Min/Max; DomainWarpGradient 0.3-0.4 cells upstream recommended. A 2D pattern node, not a cave node.
truchet-noise.port_notes: One cell window; face radii keyed by the lower cell plus axis salt so both cells agree. The 15 matchings become a tiny table indexed by hash bits (8 no-opposite + 7 with straights). The dmax clamp is required for continuity. As a cave generator it needs a junction primitive (hub), which is what bond-tunnels is.

critic.notes: The reported failure as a cave is false. The prototyper's 55 components, largest 3.5% came from NETCONN running at static init before gMatchInit, so it flood filled parallel x cylinders; the include order fix is already in the file. Re-measured on seeds it never saw (99, 2024): 21.4-21.9% void, 99.1-99.3% in a 6^3 box, 100.00% in the core of an 11^3 box (margin 3 cells). The other half of its claim holds: the tubes do not branch, they merge by overlap in the cell interior, so it only connects when fat. r .08-.14 gives 9.0% void and 9.1% largest, r .1-.17 gives 13.5% void and 9.0% largest (9.59% in the core). The look is a 2D look: even line weight, constant pitch, no bright saddle stars, which Abs(Perlin) and Abs(Simplex) do not give in my side by side, at 1.14x perlin2 scalar with defaults. 3D unwarped has the strongest lattice in the family (k=1 peak/median 60159 on seed 99 vs 4191 for bond, S-curved holes in a visible grid); under warp its cave cannot be told apart from the other tube members except for having twice the void. Trap for materials: GenTileable2D maps onto a 4D torus, and a line network in 4D misses a 2D surface. I measured that on bond (the image in bond-tunnels), not on Truchet, where the same geometry applies, so the line pattern should be expected not to tile. Shares the face hash and the clamp seam rule with bond, so it belongs as a topology choice there with a shared Output {Signed, Lines, Stripes}. AVX2 cost not measured; the 2D ~1.2 ns and 3D ~2.5 ns figures remain estimates and the 3D one looks low to me because the torus axes vary per lane.
critic.improved: No change to the kernel. Added a render, Truchet 2D lines beside real Abs(Perlin), warped Abs(Perlin), Abs(Simplex) and F2-F1 on the same seed.

tournament.notes: The reported failure as a cave is false. The prototyper's 55 components, largest 3.5% came from NETCONN running at static init before gMatchInit, so it flood filled parallel x cylinders; the include order fix is already in the file. Re-measured on seeds it never saw (99, 2024): 21.4-21.9% void, 99.1-99.3% in a 6^3 box, 100.00% in the core of an 11^3 box (margin 3 cells). The other half of its claim holds: the tubes do not branch, they merge by overlap in the cell interior, so it only connects when fat. r .08-.14 gives 9.0% void and 9.1% largest, r .1-.17 gives 13.5% void and 9.0% largest (9.59% in the core). The look is a 2D look: even line weight, constant pitch, no bright saddle stars, which Abs(Perlin) and Abs(Simplex) do not give in my side by side, at 1.14x perlin2 scalar with defaults. 3D unwarped has the strongest lattice in the family (k=1 peak/median 60159 on seed 99 vs 4191 for bond, S-curved holes in a visible grid); under warp its cave cannot be told apart from the other tube members except for having twice the void. Trap for materials: GenTileable2D maps onto a 4D torus, and a line network in 4D misses a 2D surface. I measured that on bond (the image in bond-tunnels), not on Truchet, where the same geometry applies, so the line pattern should be expected not to tile. Shares the face hash and the clamp seam rule with bond, so it belongs as a topology choice there with a shared Output {Signed, Lines, Stripes}. AVX2 cost not measured; the 2D ~1.2 ns and 3D ~2.5 ns figures remain estimates and the 3D one looks low to me because the torus axes vary per lane.

master.one_liner: Random Truchet tiles (quarter-circle arcs on a square or hex grid, tube triples on a cube) evaluated as a distance field: endless connected winding paths, mazes and 3D tunnel networks.
master.look:
Labyrinths, celtic-knot-like weaves, pipes; in 3D a fully connected random tunnel network (caves!) whose every tunnel joins another, something no distance-threshold of noise gives. Distinct from everything on the sheet.
[FaceTubes, texture-materials] Look-tested in 2D (m=12). Winding pipes with visible swelling and narrowing, continuous through cell borders, no dead ends. Warping makes intestine or worm-trail; 3D thresholded gives guaranteed connected tunnels. Connectedness is the main value for caves.
master.algorithm:
2D square: c = floor(p), f = p - c, h = hash(c). flip = h & 1 -> f.x = Select(flip, 1 - f.x, f.x). Arcs of radius 0.5 centred on corners (0,0) and (1,1): d = min(| |f| - 0.5 |, | |f - (1,1)| - 0.5 |). Arcs meet neighbours at edge midpoints, so d is continuous across cells for any random choice.
Output enum: PathDistance d; Stripe profile cos(d*Stripes*TwoPi) (multi-lane paths); Side = sign of the arc's signed distance (two-colour interlocking regions, Smith tiles: continuous regions only if the sign is chosen so colours match across edges: use the cell parity (c.x+c.y)&1 to flip the sign); Weave (Shane's over/under: 1 at |d|<w scaled by which arc is on top from bit 2).
2D hex (Shane/Fabrice): hex cell id via axial rounding (branch-free compare/select), three arcs of radius sqrt(3)/2 centred on alternating hex corners; 2 random rotations per cell (h%3) selected via Select.
3D cube (Shane's 3D Truchet): the six face centres are paired into 3 tubes; 15 pairings stored in a tiny table indexed by hash%15 (same for all lanes? no: per lane gather from a 15-entry constant table via Select chain or a 4-bit LUT). For a pair of adjacent faces the tube is a quarter torus of major radius 0.5 around the shared cube edge: d = | sqrt( (|f.a - ea|)^2... ) | i.e. d = | |(f - edgeCorner).(perp plane)| - 0.5 |; for an opposite pair it is a straight cylinder along that axis: d = |f.perp|. Take the min of 3 tube distances. Tubes exit through face centres so they connect across cells.
4D: use (x,y,z) with w selecting the hash (discontinuous in w) and document, or 4D tile with 4 tubes among 8 face centres (105 pairings table) - optional.

[TruchetNoise, lit-recent] Params: Tile enum {SmithArcs, Diagonals, Hex3Arcs, MultiScale}, LineWidth (hybrid), Depth D (int, MultiScale only), SubdivideProb (hybrid), Output enum {Distance, Mask2Colour, Stripe}.
SmithArcs 2D: c = floor(p), f = p - c, bit = hash(seed,c)&1; if bit: f.x = 1 - f.x (mirror the tile). The two arcs: circle radius 0.5 centred at (0,0) and at (1,1): d = min(| |f| - 0.5 |, | |f-(1,1)| - 0.5 |). Distance output = 1 - d/0.5 ... map to [-1,1]. Stripe: sin(2pi d/LineWidth). Mask2Colour: the Smith tile is two-colourable: colour = parity(c.x+c.y) XOR inside(arc regions) where inside = (|f|<0.5) | (|f-(1,1)|<0.5) -> gives closed blobs/regions, meandering 'maze' walls when thresholded.
Hex3Arcs: hex cell lookup (axial coords), hashed rotation among 2 states, arcs of radius 0.5 between adjacent edge midpoints.
MultiScale (Carlson): for l in 0..D-1 (fixed loop): cell at level l size 2^-l; sub = rnd01(hash(seed,l,cell)) < SubdivideProb; if !sub stop (mask 'done'); else descend. Final tile at level l*: arcs connect side points at 1/3 and 2/3 (two concentric quarter arcs radius 1/3 and 2/3 at a hashed corner, plus the 'frown/T/+' motif family chosen by hash); parity colour = (l* & 1) XOR arc-side; winged overlap handled by evaluating the 4 neighbouring tiles' arcs at the final level and taking min distance (Carlson's 'wings' = arcs extend 1/6 beyond the tile).
3D: cube cell, hash picks one of the pipe-tile orientations: quarter-torus arcs (major radius 0.5) joining 3 pairs of face centres; d = min over 3 arcs of distance to torus centreline; this is the classic 3D Truchet 'pipes' field, exact and pointwise. 4D: drop w.

[FaceTubes, texture-materials] Cell i=floor(p), f=fract(p). Hash picks a signed axis permutation applied to f (reflections and permutes via Select). In transformed cell: 2D has 2 quarter arcs at corners (0,0) and (1,1) connecting edge midpoints; 3D has 3 disjoint quarter tori along 3 mutually skew edges (standard 3D Truchet); 4D has 4 quarter arcs pairing the 8 faces. For an arc in plane (a,b) with corner c: rho=|(f_a-c_a,f_b-c_b)|, d=sqrt((rho-.5)^2+Sum others (f_o-.5)^2). Face radius: R_face=lerp(Rmin,Rmax,rnd(hash(face index, axis))), same from both cells that share the face since it is hashed by lattice coords. Arc param t=|f_b-c_b|/(|f_a-c_a|+|f_b-c_b|) (no atan). r=lerp(Ra,Rb,hermite(t)). Tube profile q=1-d/r, height sqrt(q(2-q))*r/Rmax. Output Max over arcs, or signed d-r for cave thresholds.
master.why_new: Connected curved paths with guaranteed continuity across tiles are a topological property; no amount of warping/thresholding existing noise yields closed, loop-free-or-not, connected networks. Caves via 3D Truchet are a cheap alternative to simulated tunnel systems.
master.simd_plan:
One hash per sample, no neighbour window; a handful of abs/sqrt/min and Selects. Cost ~ 0.5-1x Perlin 2D (~1 ns), 3D ~2 ns. The 15-entry pairing table becomes a sequence of Select on hash bits (or FS::Gather if available). Cube version generic over axes via 3 code paths unrolled.
[FaceTubes, texture-materials] Single cell, no window. 2D: 1 cell hash, 4 face hashes, 2 sqrt: measured 0.94x Perlin scalar. 3D: 1+6 hashes, 3 sqrt plus permutation Selects, about 1.5x Perlin 3D. 4D: 1+8 hashes, 4 arcs, about 1.5x Perlin 4D, an order of magnitude cheaper than cellular 4D. Reflection and permutation through Select on coordinate vectors works in generic GenT.
master.continuity: C0 given tube radius below about 0.35: on a face both cells measure distance to the face centre. check: c0ratio 8.00 in 2D, z-continuity fine in 3D.
master.params: Feature Scale, Variant enum {Square, Hex, Cube}, Output enum {Distance, Stripes, Side, Weave}, Stripes (int), Path Width (hybrid), Output Min/Max.
master.risks:
Visibly regular under-the-hood grid (paths always cross edges at midpoints); combine with a DomainWarp for organic look. Hex cell id needs a careful branch-free axial rounding. 4D story is weak.
[TruchetNoise, lit-recent] MultiScale 'loose ends' are only resolved by Carlson's winged overlap; a pointwise version needs the neighbour-tile evaluation to reproduce it, and the resulting multi-level mask parity logic needs care. Hex tiles need a hex lattice helper not present in FastNoise.
[FaceTubes, texture-materials] Pattern shows lattice in straight runs (axis peaks in spectrum); needs domain warp to hide it. Rmax must stay under 0.5 minus clearance for arcs to remain separated. 3D orientation table should be checked against the 2D proto: only 2D was look-tested. Another lens has a rel_truchet, so overlap is possible; radius hashing on faces is the contribution.
sources: Truchet tiling / C. S. Smith 1987 and shader-community 'Truchet' and '3D Truchet pipes' variants (recalled, not fetched)
master.variant_notes: Options merged: multi-scale Carlson tiles, 3D pipes via face pairing (PairedFaceTubes), and tube radius hashed on shared faces, so pipes swell and narrow with no seams (FaceTubes). Needs a warp to hide the grid.

spanning-tunnels.look: 2D: a maze of straight corridors with slight random tilts (jitter), dead ends everywhere in tree mode, loops in bond-graph mode; visually a near twin of bond-tunnels. 3D pipes view: straight tilted capsules meeting at jittered nodes, mine-working or scaffold like; with rot + two-octave warp it becomes a tangle of bent tubes that is hard to tell from the warped bond-tunnels image. Cave view: tube cross sections on the cut faces, nothing more. Tree mode in a 6^3 box: 67 components, largest 11.6% of the cave, so the spanning forest only coalesces far away and a view region is NOT one connected cave. Bond-graph mode p=0.5: 98.1% in one component (16 components), warped 2-octave at 8^3: 96.3% with 7 sealed pinched pockets holding 0.6%.
spanning-tunnels.dims: 2D (3x3) and 3D (3x3x3) measured; 4D would be a 3^4 window or the w-phase trick, not attempted
spanning-tunnels.range: [-1, 1], flat at +1 in rock beyond dmax = 0.5 - jit - rmax - smooth (0.19 default), no NaN, far coords fine
spanning-tunnels.artifacts: none seen (window lemma holds: bonds leaving the window are beyond dmax). Radius capped near 0.2 cells by the exactness bound.

master.one_liner: Exact signed distance to a lattice spanning forest of capsules: every cell owns a tunnel to a hashed negative-axis neighbour (plus optional loop links and chambers), so every passage belongs to an infinite connected network and the field is a true SDF.
master.look:
3D iso at 0: a Manhattan-ish but jittered network of straight-ish tunnel segments meeting at nodes, like mine workings, ant nests, root burrows or circuit-board vias; with Chamber > 0 the nodes become rooms joined by corridors; with LoopChance the forest gains cycles. DomainWarp (or DomainWarpCurl) turns it into organic burrows. 2D: a classic random labyrinth of corridors (every corridor reaches the edge, dead ends exist). Vertical cave layers: DomainAxisScale on y gives flattened stacked labyrinths.
[DirectedForestMaze, distribution-topology] At Jitter 0: a crisp perfect maze (right-angle corridors, no loops, no rooms). With jitter 0.5 and Bias 0.5: a dendritic drainage network with random tilts, like river basins or lightning; Bias toward one axis makes parallel streams joining a trunk; Diagonal gives braided 45-degree channels. Hillshaded SDF: carved channels of constant width and depth; the band mode around level w gives a single winding ribbon that fills the plane. 3D: a loop-free cave/root/vessel network (every tunnel leads out, nothing is sealed), 4D version tiles.
master.algorithm:
c = Floor(p). For each cell k in the 3x3x3 window (3x3 in 2D):
  h = Hash(k); q_k = k + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd3(h)   // Jitter <= 0.25
  axis a = pick from h (compute the 3 candidate parents k-ex, k-ey, k-ez and Select by mask), parent = k - e_a
  q_par = parent + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd3(Hash(parent))   // 27 extra hashes
  dSeg = capsuleDistance(p, q_k, q_par): t = Clamp(((p-q_k).(q_par-q_k)) / |q_par-q_k|^2, 0, 1); d = |p - q_k - t (q_par-q_k)|
  r_k = Radius * (1 + RadiusJitter * rnd11(h >> 20))
  sdf = Min(sdf, dSeg - r_k)
  optional LoopChance L: mask = ((h>>8)&255) < L*255; second link to parent2 = k - e_b (b = another axis from bits) evaluated unconditionally, folded in with Select(mask, d2 - r, BIG)
  optional Chamber: sdf = Min(sdf, |p - q_k| - ChamberRadius * rnd01(h >> 12))
Output: Signed = sdf scaled (ScaleOutput over [-Radius, ~0.7]); Solid = Clamp(1 - sdf/Radius). Seam proof: a segment of an out-of-window cell lies in the bounding box of two cell centres each within Jitter of its cell centre, hence >= 0.5 - Jitter from the sample's cell faces, so results are exact for Radius + RadiusJitter*Radius <= 0.5 - Jitter (clamp params to that). 4D: keep the 3D lattice and let w drive jitter phase: q_k += WobbleAmp * (sin(w+phi1), sin(w+phi2), sin(w+phi3)) with phi from h (table), i.e. tunnels breathe and loop in w at 3D cost (continuous in all four coords, so GenTileable2D still tiles).
master.why_new: Nothing in the graph produces 1D connected networks or exact SDFs to segments. Every tunnel connects to an infinite component (no sealed pockets), the field is Lipschitz-1 (sphere tracing, uniform wall offsets), chambers/corridors in one node, 2D doubles as a maze generator.
master.simd_plan: Cellular.inl window loop; per cell: 2 hashes, one capsule distance (~20 ops), optional second capsule and sphere; all Select-based. 3D: 27-54 capsules ~ 1.5-2.5x CellularDistance 3D (20-30 ns). 2D: 9-18 capsules ~ 1.5x CellularDistance 2D. 4D: 3D lattice + w-phase jitter (1 Sin/Cos per lane plus a phase table) ~ same as 3D; a true 3^4 window would be ~3x Cellular 4D and is not recommended.
master.continuity: C0 (min of exact capsule SDFs), gradient magnitude <= 1 everywhere.
master.params: Radius (hybrid), RadiusJitter, Jitter (<=0.25), LoopChance (0-1), ChamberRadius, Up/Down bias (prob of choosing the vertical axis as parent), WobbleAmp (4D), Feature Scale, Seed, Output enum.
master.risks:
Directed-forest topology is anisotropic (all links go toward -x/-y/-z) and reads as 'grid-like' without a warp; many leaf dead ends in the forest (no isolated pockets, but dead ends are common). Radius is capped at 0.25 cells for exactness, so wide tunnels need Feature Scale, not Radius.
[DirectedForestMaze, distribution-topology] The 'single tree' property is almost-sure and asymptotic: inside any finite view several trees that merge far away are visible, so 'all corridors in view are mutually reachable' is not guaranteed, only 'no loops, no pockets, every corridor exits the view'. Hybrid Bias changing across a cell can flip that cell's parent between samples (discontinuity) unless treated as above. Right-angled graph structure shows through even with jitter; the Diagonal option and smooth-min joins help.
master.variant_notes: DirectedForestMaze is the same forest in 2D and states the topology honestly: acyclic and pocket-free, with almost-sure coalescence only asymptotically.
